extracted.intended_audience: serious writers applying to the Community of Writers Summer Writers Workshops (fiction, nonfiction, memoir)
extracted.subtask_description: Application and submission guidelines for the Community of Writers seven-day in-person Summer Writers Workshops (fiction, nonfiction, memoir), including eligibility, manuscript formatting, deadlines, fees, and program participation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission is based on the strength and merit of the submitted manuscript and our judgment that the applicant will benefit from the workshop. We admit eighty-six writers to our fiction program and twenty-four to nonfiction/memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We make no admissions decisions before all the submissions have been read and evaluated. Acceptance notification on or before April 22, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible fiction and excluded children's books
rubrics_metrics.description: Morning workshops are devoted to Fiction; we welcome all forms of fiction, including YA, but not children’s books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying, familiarize yourself with the current teaching staff to see if you can identify people who might best serve the needs of your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible nonfiction/memoir and excluded nonfiction genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Those applying to the nonfiction program may submit memoir, narrative nonfiction, creative nonfiction, essays, and hybrid fiction/nonfiction forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary criticism, self-help, and scholarly work will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted manuscript forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission manuscript (MS) may consist of a story (or stories), essay(s) or chapter(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book chapters must include a one-page synopsis of the plot of the whole book (add to the end of MS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count limit
rubrics_metrics.description: On the first page of the MS applicants must provide the word count for submitted MS. (Excluding synopsis, MS must be less than 5,000 words.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the word count at the top center of the first page; synopsis does not count toward the 5,000-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission MS must be typed, double-spaced and 12 pt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the first page: top left indicate application program (Fiction, Nonfiction, Memoir) and what you are submitting (novel chapter(s), story or stories, essay or essays, memoir chapter(s), nonfiction book chapter(s), etc.); top center word count; top right your name in the upper right-hand corner of each page (use your actual name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not submit previously published material (print or online).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to send work currently under submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-submission policy for past applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have previously applied to our workshop, please do not submit or bring for consideration the exact same material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use previously submitted material that has been revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-category application requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying in more than one category, please send separate applications and submissions, including application fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category requires its own application and reading fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee and payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A $40 reading fee will be due with submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay online with a credit card or PayPal (a 3.25% service fee applies), or mail a check payable to Community of Writers. (Payment required for submission to be processed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission file format and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a digital file (PDF or Word.doc) of your submission MS to the online application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital files will be deleted after workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and timeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for receipt of application/submission: before midnight, March 10, 2026 (before midnight PST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance notification: on or before April 22, 2026; deposit due May 1, 2026; tuition balance due on or before July 1, 2026; registration/first day of conference July 10, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit and tuition payment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit of $1000 is due upon acceptance. (Awards of financial aid may reduce this amount.) Tuition is $1,900 (tuition may change slightly without notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit is nonrefundable. Tuition does not include housing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who require financial aid to attend should request it in the application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our organization intends to raise funds and try to provide whatever level of financial aid is necessary to compensate for tuition increases; view Financial Aid Information for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing arrangement and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition does not include housing; CW can arrange lodging at the Village at Palisades Tahoe or private houses and will reserve on first-request basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Room type availability is limited; however, the organization guarantees housing to everyone who would like them to arrange it. CW-arranged lodging payment due May 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop structure and participant expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Morning workshops meet daily from 8:30-11:30; each workshop consists of roughly 12 participants and has a new workshop leader each day. During the course of the week, one manuscript by each participant is critiqued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are asked to arrive with copies of the manuscript they would like treated in workshop. Participants may need to set aside time for the reading and evaluation of workshop manuscripts. Except for a mid-week afternoon off, participants may attend over six hours of programming each day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual conference policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant is assigned a brief one-on-one conference with a staff member appropriate to the submitted manuscript. These conferences usually run no longer than twenty minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most cases, the manuscript to be discussed will be the one submitted with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second manuscript for individual conference
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the manuscript which participants have treated in morning workshop, they may have a second manuscript read by a staff member who meets with them in an individual conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an opportunity for additional feedback outside the primary workshop manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returnee attendance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Past Writers Workshop participants have specific reattendance rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction Alums: Attendance is allowed 2 out of every 3 years. Nonfiction Alums: Attendance is allowed after you have taken 2 years off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special classes and seminar availability and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Special afternoon classes and seminars (e.g., The Alchemy of Adaptation; The Book Proposal) are offered to enrolled participants, often for an additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Alchemy of Adaptation class: $250 fee. The Book Proposal seminar (Samuel Freedman): $200 fee; open only to those enrolled in the Writers Workshops who write memoir or nonfiction. Open Workshop led by Sands Hall: no additional fee. Indicate interest on the application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program confidentiality and file deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital submission files are deleted after workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that files will not be retained long-term by the program.
